title: noo-addon-node-workloads/1: an add-on's node workloads (node-workloads.json)
description: A file of the add-on's signed bundle, listed in the bundle lock beside resources.json and routes.json. Core builds the container from this closed declaration and places it on a capable node; the add-on never supplies a ref, a mount, a capability or a free-form env. Validated by the CLI (noo-cli/src/addons/decls.rs), the gateway (gateway-rust/src/addon_workloads.rs) and the node agent (node-agent-go/internal/nodewl), each against tests/fixtures/i300/node-workloads/ (cases.json lists the stable refusal code for each). The door's DNS SAN noo-stunnel-<addon>-<workload> must be one DNS label of at most 63 characters, so a node workload is refused when len(addon) + 1 + len(workload) > 51. JSON null is refused on every field (this format has no nullable field), and so is a repeated object key; every validator must match. Contract: docs/reference/node-workloads.md. Design: noomesh-internal proposals/i300 section 4.1.

target.description: A container path. Never / (the pattern needs a component).

oneOf.description: An integer range. A value is a base-10 integer string in desired-config.
An enum of strings. Booleans are {"one_of": ["false"]}.

name.description: One DNS label piece of the door name noo-stunnel-<addon>-<workload>: lower-case letters, digits and -, no leading or trailing -. len(addon)+1+len(workload) <= 51 (x-noo-rules).

image.description: A NAME in the signed lock's images map, never a ref (x-noo-rules).

uid.description: 0 is refused. Never the image's default user.

path.description: POSTed by the node agent through the door.

x-noo-rules: image names a key of the signed lock's images map; an unknown name is refused (image_not_in_lock). The digest comes from the lock, so the bundle signature covers it.
workload names are unique within the file (name_duplicate).

door name: the door's DNS SAN is noo-stunnel-<addon>-<workload>, which must be ONE DNS label of at most 63 characters, so a node workload is refused when len(addon) + 1 + len(workload) > 51 (door_name_too_long). Both the workload name (above) and the add-on name must match ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$ (door_name_invalid): _, upper case and a leading or trailing - are refused, and _ is never mapped to - (a per-file validator cannot see a collision between two add-ons). The add-on name is known only at validation, so it is not a schema check.

env keys must start with <ADDON_UPPER>_ (the add-on name upper-cased, - as _), with the addon known at validation (env_key_outside_prefix). Refused prefixes win over the add-on prefix: NOO_, NVIDIA_, CUDA_, LD_, PYTHON, HF_, TRANSFORMERS_ (env_key_refused_prefix, stated above in propertyNames).

an env bound with min and max needs min <= max (env_bound_invalid). Values in desired-config are strings: an integer bound takes a base-10 integer string, an enum takes one of its members, a boolean is {"one_of": ["false"]}.

scratch targets are not /, /proc, /sys or /dev (or below them), are unique, and neither equal, inside nor around any model slot target (scratch_target_refused, scratch_invalid, scratch_in_model_slot).
model slot names and targets are unique, and no slot target is inside another (model_slot_invalid).
the agent mounts each chosen set read-only at its slot target, as one directory; many=true slots mount each set under <target>/<set id>; optional=true slots may stay empty.

JSON null is refused on every field with field_type (the schema's types already refuse it; Go's decoder would read `"gpu": null` as 0). This format has no nullable field. A repeated object key is refused with duplicate_key.
an unknown field is refused everywhere (unknown_field); a CLI from before a minor addition refuses the lock rather than half-reading it.
